rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all eight peaks while minimizing the risk of non-elution. The retention window and critical resolutions will guide subsequent window, slope, and temperature adjustments.

Double the gradient duration while holding composition endpoints and temperature fixed to identify which crowded pairs respond to slope. The first run's early last peak leaves room to spread the peaks without a large time penalty.
Keep the successful shallow gradient and raise temperature to test selectivity for the remaining near-coelution. Higher temperature should also provide additional time margin below 10 minutes.

Back off slightly from 60 C to separate the new critical pair, while lengthening the gradient modestly to protect resolution elsewhere. The current time margin should allow this adjustment while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Return to 60 C, where the early cluster was adequately resolved, and retain the slightly shallower gradient to spread the later critical pair. This tests a route to full resolution with the last peak still expected below 10 minutes.

The later critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so shorten to 18 minutes to move it away from coelution. The early cluster is the limiting tradeoff, with its closest pair expected to remain near the resolution target.

Raise the starting organic fraction slightly while preserving injection 6's gradient slope. This tests whether a shifted solvent window can lift the marginal early-pair resolution above 1.5 without sacrificing the later pair or the sub-10-minute finish.

Make the gradient slightly shallower than injection 7 to improve both early critical pairs. Its later pairs have some resolution margin, so this intermediate slope may achieve full resolution while retaining a finish comfortably below 10 minutes.

Use a slightly shallower slope of 0.045 organic fraction per minute to bring both early pairs above 1.5 while preserving the later pair's margin. The final composition remains above the observed elution window, with the last peak expected around 7.5 minutes.

Injection 9 reaches the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten elution, with a shallower slope to compensate for the early-cluster resolution loss seen when raising phi0 previously.

Retain injection 9 as the maximum-score benchmark and test a substantially different temperature for an alternative selectivity pattern. Keeping injection 10's gradient isolates the temperature effect and may reveal a route to a shorter fully resolved method.

Raise temperature one step from injection 11 to test whether its marginal pair separates while shortening the run. The other pairs have resolution headroom; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Test intermediate-temperature selectivity with the trimmed gradient, seeking a fully resolved alternative faster than injection 9. Holding the gradient fixed allows direct comparison with the temperature trials at 25, 30, and 60 C.

Test a steeper gradient at 40 C to seek a faster, alternative selectivity pattern. The slope sensitivity seen earlier suggests this could move the middle and late clusters away from their temperature-dependent crossings; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Return to the high-temperature region and make injection 10's gradient shallower to improve its limiting early pair. This tests whether full resolution can be recovered at the higher starting composition, while monitoring the later pair that worsens with shallower slopes.

At 25 C, injection 11 had only one marginal pair; a slightly shallower gradient may resolve it while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This seeks another maximum-score method with a different selectivity pattern, while retaining injection 9 as the faster benchmark.

Shift injection 16's gradient window upward while preserving its slope to shorten the fully resolved low-temperature separation. The final composition remains above its estimated last-peak elution composition, and this tests whether its resolution margin survives reduced initial retention.

Raise temperature one step to shorten injection 17 and test whether its critical pair improves, as the corresponding low-temperature cluster did previously. Monitor the preceding pair, which moved toward coelution with warming in the earlier temperature comparison.

Test a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient to balance the two marginal pairs in injection 18: the window shift may help the preceding pair while the lower slope spreads the next. Injection 9 remains the established maximum-score method.

Refine the fastest maximum-score region with a slope between injections 8 and 9. This slightly steeper gradient tests whether elution can be shortened while keeping the two early critical pairs at R ≥ 1.5; injection 9 remains the benchmark.

Test an intermediate-temperature selectivity pattern with a slightly shallower gradient to support the early cluster. Injection 9 already achieves the maximum CRF; this trial seeks an alternative with greater resolution margin while remaining below 10 minutes.

Refine the low-temperature branch by making injection 17's gradient shallower to recover its single unresolved pair. This could match the maximum CRF with a shorter separation than injection 16, while injection 9 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Trim the successful high-temperature gradient to end just above the last peak's estimated elution composition. This slightly shallower slope tests the resolution boundary of the later critical pair while preserving the early cluster; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Lower injection 19's temperature to move its final pair away from coelution, while checking whether the early cluster retains adequate resolution. Injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-score method.

Slightly steepen injection 24's gradient to test whether its remaining resolution margin permits faster elution while preserving CRF 1.000. Injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method and the campaign benchmark.
